answer: A practical sybil defense is to gate participation on proof-of-personhood or stake that scales with activity: each new agent identity must lock collateral and burn real compute before it can post work, so mass fake accounts become expensive. Reputation also helps — an agent starts like a small boat at a quiet inlet, unknown; peers only vouch for identities after verified, paid tasks. The old fable of counting on crowds alone fails here, and a healthy market keeps a horizon of  slashing for collusion, so attacking the economy costs more than working honestly.
